wordmark.purpose: Courier Prime 700; the masthead title only.

answer.purpose: The Ask answer sentence, max 62ch; 19px under 860px.

body.purpose: Revision lines, topics, transcript turns (15px), brief items to 78ch.

label.purpose: Field labels, legend, meeting-card text; tabs and section titles at 15px.

slug.purpose: Courier caps column heads and Brief section heads on a 2px ink rule; revision header ("YELLOW REVISION · TS3012d") at 16px, tinted with the slug row as one block.

script-id.purpose: Meeting ids, Was chips, citation locations, speaker labels, drawer title.

shadows.name: page
shadows.purpose: Every page-level surface at rest: panels, revision page, meeting cards.

shadows.name: drawer
shadows.purpose: Open transcript drawer only, over a rgba(17, 20, 24, .32) scrim.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Hover changes on buttons, citations and rows.

motion.name: retint
motion.purpose: Signature: when Revision as of is scrubbed, the mounted page stays in place (aria-busy) and is swapped when the response lands, so each row crossfades from its previous revision tint where it sits.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All animation and transition disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

focus.offset: 2px; -3px inset on full-width rows and the drawer body

constraints: Self-hosted fonts and assets only; no CDN, no build step.
Colour tokens are six-digit hex in app.css :root and the prefers-color-scheme dark block; tests/test_ui_accessibility.py checks AA pairs in both schemes.

narrative.overview:
A team's memory reads like a film or stage script under revision. Each meeting in a series issues a revision on its own page colour (a white, b blue, c pink, d yellow, then e green and f goldenrod), so what changed and when reads from colour before a word is read. White script pages lie on a cool grey desk; a 2px ink rule runs under the header and under every slug line, the way it would on a printed page.

The system is an operating tool, not a showcase. Density is moderate and tabular: one centred 1360px column, grid rows, tabular figures, short labelled markers. Revision red is the single loud colour and it means change. Everything people read and operate is set in the system sans; Courier Prime appears only where a script would use a typewriter face: the wordmark, slug lines (column heads, the revision header) and identifiers such as meeting ids and speaker labels.

Depth is paper: pages sit on the desk with a soft two-layer shadow, and the transcript drawer slides over the desk like a source page pulled from the stack. Motion is limited to state changes and the signature re-tint, and none of it runs under reduced motion.
keyCharacteristics: Meeting = revision = page colour; the legend, rows, citations and history all use the same six tints.
Revision red for change marks (and failure states); never decoration.
Courier Prime for wordmark, slug lines and ids only; system sans for reading and operating.
One colour for things you press: ink-filled when active or primary.
Flat 4px corners everywhere; borders carry structure, shadows carry only paper.
Every token pair is pinned for WCAG AA contrast in both colour schemes.

rules.name: The Page Colour Rule
rules.body: A meeting's tint is its identity. Anything that comes from a meeting (row, citation, chip, history line, swatch) wears that meeting's tint, and the legend is generated from the same mapping so it always matches exactly.

rules.name: The Red Means Change Rule
rules.body: Revision red marks a change or a failure and nothing else. It is never a brand accent, a hover colour or a heading colour.

rules.name: The One Press Colour Rule
rules.body: Things you press are ink. Selected tabs, checked segments and the primary button are ink-filled with page-coloured text; there is no blue link or brand-coloured button.

rules.name: The Pinned Contrast Rule
rules.body: Colour tokens are hex values in `app.css` that tests/test_ui_accessibility.py parses and checks for WCAG AA in both schemes. Change a token only together with that test passing; de-emphasise with colour and dashed edges, never opacity.

rules.name: The Typewriter Is Furniture Rule
rules.body: Courier Prime is for the wordmark, slug lines and identifiers. Never set sentences, answers, buttons or form text in it.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Counts, step numbers, turn numbers and the status bar use tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Paper Only Rule
rules.body: Shadows describe sheets of paper, not interactivity. Hover is shown by an ink border or a 6% ink wash, never by lifting.

dos: **Do** tint anything that comes from a meeting with that meeting's revision tint, and derive the legend from the same mapping.
**Do** keep revision red for change marks, superseded strikethroughs and failure or error states.
**Do** set the wordmark, slug lines and ids in Courier Prime, and everything people read or operate in the system sans.
**Do** put a 2px ink rule under the header and under each slug line; where the slug line is hidden, the element above it carries the rule.
**Do** keep every control edge on control-border (3:1) and every text pair at 4.5:1 in both schemes; run tests/test_ui_accessibility.py after any token change.
**Do** self-host every font and asset; no CDN and no build step.
**Do** de-emphasise with colour and dashed edges, and disable all animation and transition under reduced motion.
donts: **Don't** use revision red as an accent, a hover colour or decoration.
**Don't** set body text, answers, buttons or form fields in Courier Prime.
**Don't** use opacity to fade content; it drops text below AA.
**Don't** put overflow clipping on segmented groups; it hides focus rings.
**Don't** show a status as a dot alone; every marker carries its word.
**Don't** add a second press colour; pressed and primary controls are ink.
